Write questions and answers from a document set

Source: R/questions.R
dragon_questions.Rd

Turns documents into training data. For each chunk a model writes a few self-contained questions and answers them from that chunk alone; simple deterministic filters then mark pairs that are not grounded in the chunk, name things the chunk does not, refer to "the passage", or duplicate another question. Nothing is dropped: every pair comes back with keep and, when rejected, a reason, so you can review them (the Documents tab has a screen for it) before training with dragon_questions_dataset().

Usage

dragon_questions(
  docs,
  generator = NULL,
  n_per_chunk = 3,
  mix = TRUE,
  include_quotes = FALSE,
  include_code = TRUE,
  include_changelog = FALSE,
  load_in_4bit = "auto",
  batch_size = 4,
  max_new_tokens = 420,
  wait = TRUE
)

dragon_questions_progress(job)

dragon_questions_wait(job)

Arguments

docs

A dragon_documents object or its directory.

generator

What writes the pairs. NULL uses the local model recommended for this machine (see dragon_check()); a model id uses that local model; a teacher such as dragon_llm_anthropic(), an ellmer chat, a run, or any function from prompts to replies is called from R instead. Local generation runs as a background Python process.

n_per_chunk

Questions asked for per chunk.

mix

Ask for a mix of question types: one "what" or "which", one "why" or "how", and, where the passage compares two things, one "how do they differ". On FDA guidance this raised comparison questions from 11 to 98 of the kept pairs and why/how questions from 113 to 142, kept 81 percent of pairs instead of 89, and a 3B trained on either set answered the same 23 of 24 test questions. FALSE asks for any three questions.

include_quotes, include_code, include_changelog

Which chunks to use. Block quotes are skipped by default (a quoted example reply is not your policy), code blocks are included, changelog-like sources are skipped.

load_in_4bit

For a local generator: "auto", TRUE, or FALSE; see dragon_backend_local().

batch_size, max_new_tokens

Local generation settings.

wait

Block until done. With FALSE, a local generation returns a job to poll with dragon_questions_progress() and finish with dragon_questions_wait(); a teacher always runs to completion.

job

A job from dragon_questions(wait = FALSE).

Value

A dragon_questions data frame: id, chunk_id, source, section, question, answer, keep, reason, decided_by, with the file it was saved to in attr(, "path") and the set in attr(, "documents"). Edit keep and dragon_questions_save() it.

Details

Review them. On the package's own documentation about 60 percent of a 7B model's pairs were usable, 33 percent of a 3B's, 20 percent of a 1.5B's, and a fifth of what passed the filters was still wrong or trivial. Quoted material and changelog-like sources are skipped by default because they produced the worst pairs.

Examples

if (interactive()) {
docs <- dragon_documents("policies/")
qa <- dragon_questions(docs)                      # local model, background, waits
qa                                                # how many kept, and why not
qa$keep[qa$id == "p0007"] <- TRUE                 # rescue one after reading it
dragon_questions_save(qa)
ds <- dragon_questions_dataset(qa, docs)          # excerpts retrieved into every prompt
run <- dragon_train(ds, "Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct", wait = TRUE)
}
